summary.name: 3D printing
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing 3D printing (additive manufacturing): building three-dimensional objects layer by layer from a CAD or digital 3D model, covering its terminology, history, and benefits.
use_cases: Understanding what 3D printing and additive manufacturing mean
Researching the history of 3D printing technologies
Comparing FDM, SLA and SLS printing processes
Learning about 3D printing in aerospace and medicine
Background reading on open-source RepRap-style printers
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article rather than a software tool. It defines 3D printing as building objects from a CAD or digital 3D model by depositing, joining or solidifying material under computer control, typically layer by layer. It explains the terms 3D printing and additive manufacturing and how standards bodies distinguish them. It traces the technology's history from 1940s science fiction and 1970s–1980s patents through the FDM patent expiry in 2009, the RepRap project, and recent medical and aerospace uses. It also covers benefits such as complex geometry, reduced waste and lower-cost prototyping.
notable: Covers the history of 3D printing from 1945 science fiction to modern industrial use
Explains how standards bodies distinguish 3D printing from additive manufacturing
Notes that FDM is the most common process and that FDM patents expired in 2009
Describes the open-source RepRap project that aimed to print many of its own parts
caveats: Encyclopedic overview only; it does not describe software or a downloadable tool
Some claims are marked as needing citations, such as the origin of the powder bed inkjet term
